brief_summary: Horizontal strip of six small keycap glyphs naming the extra key positions ISO and JIS layouts carry that ANSI does not: the ISO extra key (shared by ISO and JIS), and four JIS-only keys — Yen, Ro, Muhenkan, Henkan, and Kana. Each glyph is marked amber and labeled with which layout(s) require it, illustrating that an ANSI keycap set has no keycap for any of these positions.
data_sources: ansi-iso-jis-keyboard-layout-guide.mdx § 'The three layouts, physically' — 'use the freed-up space for an extra key between Left Shift and Z — a key ANSI simply doesn't have'
ansi-iso-jis-keyboard-layout-guide.mdx § 'The three layouts, physically' — 'JIS also splits the area near Backspace and the right-hand Shift to add a Yen key ... and a Ro key beside the right Shift'
ansi-iso-jis-keyboard-layout-guide.mdx § 'The three layouts, physically' — 'commonly labeled Muhenkan, Henkan, and Kana on a JP legend set'
ansi-iso-jis-keyboard-layout-guide.mdx § 'Why this gates keycap-set compatibility' — 'there's no ANSI keycap at all for the extra ISO key, because ANSI doesn't have that key position'
